In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MMPI-168 profile of asymptomatic HIV-1 positive gay men was clinically elevated, with the most common profile configuration being the 4-9-2 code type.
the MMPI profiles of HIV-1 infected subjects were not significantly different from profiles of seronegative gay men.
MMPI-168 data do not support the notion that all HIV-1 seroconverters are psychologically distressed or that they are psychologically similar to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMPI profiles of HIV-1 seronegative gay men are similar to MMPI profiles of asymptomatic HIV-1 gay men.
, in contrast to the mean profiles of seropositives, individual profiles are not significantly different from those of the seronegative gay controls.
, in general, MMPI profiles of seropositives are elevated and that there is no evidence for a single MMPI profile for seropositive individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MMPI is a useful instrument to assess emotional distress in HIV-infected gay men, and it may be useful to assess emotional distress and psychological functioning in HIV-infected persons from other populations as well.
MMPI codes should be considered in the context of the person's life situation.
MMPI profiles are not useful for predicting the presence or absence of HIV infection in gay men.
